findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hard-coded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables. These credentials are stored unencrypted in the Terraform state and function configuration, exposing them to anyone with read access to the Lambda console, API, or state file.

The Lambda function does not specify a KMS key (kms_key_arn) for encrypting environment variables at rest, so sensitive values like the embedded access keys are protected only by the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed key with tighter access control, weakening encryption-at-rest guarantees for secrets.
The function uses nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Node.js runtime no longer receiving security patches from AWS, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime itself.
